s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the predominant sector and area associated with disguised unemployment?
x: Disguised unemployment is predominantly found in agriculture, especially on family farms in rural areas.
tq: Use the sector-area pair rather than relying only on the name of the unemployment type.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Seasonal unemployment is common in agriculture, tourism and agro-industries.
2. Educated unemployment is predominantly an urban phenomenon.
3. Structural unemployment is generally short-term and temporary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because structural unemployment is long-run in nature.
tq: Identify the duration trap in the statement describing structural unemployment.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Type of unemployment)
A. Seasonal
B. Technological
C. Cyclical
D. Structural

List-II (Predominant area or condition)
1. Manufacturing and routine services
2. Industry and services during recession
3. Whole economy over the long run
4. Agriculture, tourism and agro-industries

Select the correct code:
x: Seasonal unemployment is associated with agriculture, tourism and agro-industries; technological unemployment with manufacturing and routine services; cyclical unemployment with recession-hit industry and services; and structural unemployment with the whole economy over the long run.
tq: Start from the sure pairs and eliminate codes with a misplaced sector.

s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes rural and urban unemployment in India?
o: Educated unemployment is mainly rural, whereas disguised unemployment is mainly urban.
Seasonal and disguised unemployment are associated mainly with rural areas, whereas educated unemployment is mainly urban.
Structural unemployment is confined to agriculture, whereas technological unemployment is confined to tourism.
Cyclical unemployment occurs only in rural areas, whereas seasonal unemployment occurs only in cities.
x: NCERT identifies seasonal and disguised unemployment as major rural forms, while educated unemployment is predominantly urban.
tq: Compare the rural and urban pairs directly instead of matching one type with one area only.

s: With reference to open unemployment in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correct according to the PLFS figures for 2023–24?
o: The rural rate was 5.9% and the urban rate was 3.4%.
The rural rate was 3.4% and the urban rate was 5.9%.
Both rural and urban rates were 3.4%.
Both rural and urban rates were 5.9%.
x: The PLFS figures cited for Andhra Pradesh in 2023–24 place open unemployment at 3.4% in rural areas and 5.9% in urban areas.
tq: Read the rural-urban comparison carefully; open unemployment differs from broader rural seasonal unemployment.

s: Which one of the following is the defining test for identifying disguised unemployment?
o: Withdrawal of some workers leaves total output unchanged.
Workers remain unemployed throughout the business cycle.
Workers change jobs frequently in search of higher wages.
Withdrawal of some workers causes output to double.
x: Disguised unemployment is identified when removing some workers does not reduce total output, implying zero marginal productivity of those workers.
tq: Apply the marginal-productivity test to the employment situation.

s: In a family farm, eight persons work on land that requires only five persons, and removal of three workers does not reduce total output. This situation represents
x: The surplus workers appear employed but have zero marginal productivity because their withdrawal leaves total output unchanged.
tq: Use the output-after-withdrawal condition to identify hidden unemployment.

s:
Consider the following statements about disguised unemployment:
1. It is a form of hidden rather than open unemployment.
2. It is commonly observed among family members working on agricultural holdings.
3. Its marginal productivity of labour may be zero or negative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Disguised unemployment is hidden unemployment, is common on family farms, and involves zero or negative marginal productivity for surplus workers.
tq: Check each defining feature before selecting the comprehensive option.

s: Which one of the following is a distinguishing feature of disguised unemployment in relation to PLFS headline unemployment rates?
o: It is fully captured because all workers report themselves as unemployed.
It is captured only during the contraction phase of the business cycle.
It is generally not captured because the persons appear to be employed.
It is measured exclusively through urban establishment surveys.
x: Persons in disguised unemployment appear employed, so this hidden form is not captured by headline unemployment rates in the same way as open unemployment.
tq: Distinguish apparent employment from measured open unemployment.

s: Cyclical unemployment arises primarily from
o: The seasonal closure of agricultural activities
A fall in aggregate demand for goods and services
The time taken to search for a new job
A mismatch between acquired skills and available jobs
x: Cyclical unemployment results from deficient aggregate demand during recession or depression, leading firms to reduce employment.
tq: Match the unemployment type with its immediate macroeconomic cause.
sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

s: Cyclical unemployment is most closely associated with which phase of the business cycle?
x: Cyclical unemployment is linked to the contraction or trough phase and begins to decline when recovery or boom starts.
tq: Link the cause of unemployment to the correct business-cycle phase.
sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): Cyclical unemployment tends to decline when economic recovery begins.
Reason (R): Recovery is generally accompanied by an improvement in aggregate demand for goods and services.

Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true, and the rise in aggregate demand during recovery encourages firms to restore production and employment.
tq: Check whether the macroeconomic reason directly explains the movement in cyclical unemployment.
sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

s: According to Keynes, unemployment in developed economies primarily results from
o: A mismatch caused only by technological change
x: Keynes explained unemployment in developed economies mainly through deficiency in effective demand, which is associated with demand-deficient or cyclical unemployment.
tq: Associate the economist with the precise explanation rather than a related unemployment type.
sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following best describes the basic nature of unemployment in India?
o: Predominantly technological and confined to manufacturing
Predominantly structural and long-run in character
Entirely cyclical and confined to recessions
x: Indian unemployment is basically structural because the demand for labour falls short of supply over the long run due to several structural factors.
tq: Separate the broad national character of unemployment from sector-specific forms.
sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

s: Which combination best explains the structural nature of unemployment in India?
o: Only seasonal rainfall variations and tourism cycles
High labour mobility, labour-intensive production and low population growth
Rapid population growth, labour immobility and a shift towards capital-intensive production
Short job-search periods and temporary workplace transfers
x: Rapid population growth, labour immobility and the shift towards capital-intensive production contribute to a long-run shortfall of labour demand relative to supply.
tq: Select the option containing the structural causes rather than temporary causes.
sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a structural cause of unemployment in India identified in the context of the secondary sector?
o: Jobless growth and inadequate focus on MSMEs
Rapid expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing generating abundant jobs
Slow infrastructure and delays in official paperwork
Neglected structural transformation of the secondary sector
x: Rapid expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing generating abundant jobs would reduce, rather than cause, structural unemployment. The other factors are identified structural impediments.
tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated structural cause.
sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding unemployment in India:
1. A large agricultural workforce contributes to seasonal and disguised unemployment.
2. Indian unemployment differs from the demand-deficient unemployment emphasised by Keynes for developed economies.
3. Underemployment is also a feature of the Indian labour market.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. India has substantial seasonal, disguised and underemployment, while its basic unemployment problem is structural rather than solely Keynesian demand deficiency.
tq: Combine the sectoral, theoretical and labour-market dimensions before choosing the code.
sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following combinations reflects other causes associated with unemployment in India?
o: A complete shift towards labour-intensive manufacturing and export-led growth
Universal formal employment, high female labour force participation and perfect skill matching
Only temporary job search and absence of capital-intensive sectors
Skill-curriculum mismatch, a predominantly informal workforce and low female labour force participation
x: Skill-curriculum mismatch, approximately 90% informal employment and low female labour force participation are among the stated causes. Capital-intensive growth and limited export orientation also contribute to the problem.
tq: Choose the option that groups multiple related structural labour-market weaknesses.
sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

s: Growth led mainly by capital-intensive IT and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing is associated with
o: The conversion of cyclical unemployment into frictional unemployment
A source of employment-generation limitations in India
The disappearance of underemployment in rural areas
A reduction in structural unemployment through mass job creation
x: Capital-intensive growth in sectors such as IT and finance does not generate employment on the scale of labour-intensive manufacturing, thereby contributing to employment limitations.
tq: Apply the labour-intensity distinction to the employment effect of growth.
sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

s: Educated unemployment in India is predominantly associated with urban areas mainly because
o: Education automatically causes workers to leave the labour force.
Agricultural work is unavailable in every rural month.
Urban workers are excluded from all formal employment.
Educated persons are unable to find jobs matching their qualifications and industry requirements.
x: Educated unemployment is an urban phenomenon in which qualified persons fail to find employment matching their education and the needs of industry.
tq: Connect the location of educated unemployment with the qualification-job mismatch.

s: According to the India Skills Report 2024 figure cited, approximately what proportion of graduates was considered employable?
x: The cited India Skills Report 2024 estimate places the employability of graduates at approximately 46%.
tq: Retain the precise percentage instead of substituting a rounded majority figure.

s: According to PLFS 2025, the unemployment rate for persons with secondary schooling and above was
x: The cited PLFS 2025 figure for persons with secondary schooling and above was 6.5%, more than double the national rate.
tq: Use the exact education-linked unemployment figure and compare nearby alternatives.

s: For persons with secondary schooling and above, the PLFS 2025 unemployment rate was reported as
o: Higher in rural areas than in urban areas, at 7.2% and 5.9%, respectively
Equal in rural and urban areas, at 6.5% each
Higher in rural areas than in urban areas, at 7.2% and 6%, respectively
Higher in urban areas than in rural areas, at 7.2% and 6%, respectively
x: The cited PLFS 2025 rates were 7.2% in urban areas and 6% in rural areas for persons with secondary schooling and above.
tq: Compare both the direction and the values of the rural-urban figures.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the cited PLFS 2025 unemployment rates for youth aged 18–29 and for tertiary-educated youth, respectively?
x: The cited PLFS 2025 unemployment rate was 14.8% for youth aged 18–29 and rose to 29.4% for tertiary-educated youth.
tq: Keep the population groups separate when comparing closely related percentages.

s: What proportion of tertiary-educated youth was reported to be NEET in PLFS 2025?
x: The cited PLFS 2025 figure was 40.1% of tertiary-educated youth being NEET, meaning not in employment, education or training.
tq: Distinguish the NEET percentage from the unemployment percentages for the same broad group.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the cited unemployment rates among Gen Z graduates?
x: The cited figures for Gen Z graduates were 29% for males and 36.9% for females.
tq: Check the gender labels before comparing the two percentages.

s: The unemployment rate cited for Gen Z persons aged 15–26 was
x: The cited unemployment rate for Gen Z persons aged 15–26 was 11.9%.
tq: Match the age group with its own rate rather than using the youth aggregate figure.

s: A person working fewer than the normal number of hours is an example of
x: Visible underemployment involves working fewer than normal hours. It can be observed directly from the amount of work performed.
tq: Use the observable-hours distinction to separate visible from invisible underemployment.

s: An MBA graduate working full-time as a driver at a very low income is an example of
x: Invisible underemployment exists when a person works full-time but earns very little or works below their ability, as in the example of an MBA working as a driver.
tq: Look beyond the number of hours and identify underutilisation of skills or income.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes frictional unemployment from structural unemployment?
o: Frictional unemployment requires structural reform, whereas structural unemployment ends with a short job search.
Frictional unemployment exists only during depression, whereas structural unemployment disappears during recession.
Frictional unemployment is short-term job-search unemployment, whereas structural unemployment is long-term skill-job mismatch.
Frictional unemployment is caused by technology, whereas structural unemployment is caused by seasonal agriculture.
x: Frictional unemployment results from the temporary time lag involved in changing or searching for jobs, while structural unemployment is long-term and arises from a mismatch between skills and available jobs.
tq: Separate the two types using cause and duration together.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Frictional unemployment can exist even when the economy is at full employment.
2. Structural unemployment is deep-rooted and may require reskilling or structural reform.
3. Frictional unemployment is generally permanent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because frictional unemployment is normally short-term and temporary.
tq: Use the duration and policy-response contrast to reject the reversed statement.

s: A worker voluntarily leaves a job and spends a short period searching for a better one. This is an example of
x: The temporary gap caused by quitting one job and searching for another is frictional or search unemployment.
tq: Identify the unemployment type from the worker's transition between jobs.

s: Which situation best illustrates structural unemployment?
o: A firm laying off workers during a recession
A worker changing jobs after voluntarily quitting
A farm worker remaining idle during the agricultural off-season
A labour-intensive economy shifting towards capital-intensive production
x: A shift from labour-intensive to capital-intensive production changes the demand for labour and creates a long-term structural mismatch.
tq: Match the example to long-term structural change rather than a temporary interruption.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Frictional unemployment — needs immediate structural reform
Frictional unemployment — normal even at full employment
Structural unemployment — exists only during economic boom
x: Frictional unemployment is a normal feature that can exist even at full employment. Structural unemployment is long-run and deep-rooted, not a temporary search gap or a boom-only phenomenon.
tq: Find the correctly matched pair after rejecting reversed definitions and durations.

s: A person who is able and willing to work but does not get any job is experiencing which type of unemployment?
x: Open unemployment exists when a person is willing and able to work but has no job at all.
tq: Distinguish the direct definition from closely related classifications.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: Which one of the following best describes hidden or disguised unemployment?
o: Workers are temporarily dismissed during a recession
Workers refuse jobs because the prevailing wage is low
Persons appear to be employed but make no effective contribution to output
Workers change jobs while searching for a better match
x: In hidden or disguised unemployment, persons appear to be employed, but their removal does not reduce output because they contribute nothing or very little to production.
tq: Separate apparent employment from actual productive contribution.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s:
Consider the following statements regarding voluntary and involuntary unemployment:
1. Voluntary unemployment occurs when a person is unwilling to work at the prevailing wage.
2. Involuntary unemployment occurs when a person is willing to work at the prevailing wage but cannot find a job.
3. The labour force counts only voluntary unemployment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The labour force counts involuntary unemployment, not only voluntary unemployment.
tq: Find the statement that reverses the voluntary–involuntary distinction.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s:
Which of the following may lead to voluntary unemployment?
1. High benefits that reduce the incentive to accept work
2. A high marginal tax rate
3. Waiting for a better-suited job
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: High benefits, a high marginal tax rate and waiting for a better-suited job are all stated causes of voluntary unemployment.
tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed cause belongs to the same category.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: Unemployment that persists over a long period is generally classified as:
x: Chronic unemployment is long-term unemployment that persists over an extended period.
tq: Match the duration-based description with the exact term.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Unemployment trap — unemployment caused by seasonal agricultural activity
Casual unemployment — unemployment lasting for more than twelve months
Long-term unemployment — unemployment arising only from a temporary recession
Classical unemployment — unemployment caused by wages being too high
x: Classical, or real-wage, unemployment occurs when wages are too high. Long-term unemployment refers to unemployment exceeding twelve months, while casual unemployment involves day-to-day contract work and an unemployment trap may arise when benefits discourage work.
tq: Check the exact cause attached to each similar unemployment term.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: A worker employed on a day-to-day contract basis is most appropriately associated with:
x: Casual employment is based on day-to-day contract work; the classification is distinct from chronic and classical unemployment.
tq: Apply the employment arrangement rather than the duration or wage condition.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: A person who has remained unemployed for more than 12 months falls under which category?
x: Long-term unemployment is defined here as unemployment lasting for more than twelve months.
tq: Use the stated time threshold to identify the classification.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: Which situation illustrates an unemployment trap?
o: Benefits discourage a person from accepting available work
Automation replaces a routine manufacturing task
A worker changes jobs while searching for a better match
A recession reduces aggregate demand for labour
x: An unemployment trap occurs when benefits reduce the incentive to work and discourage acceptance of available employment.
tq: Identify the classification from its behavioural mechanism.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s:
With reference to full employment, consider the following statements:
1. Every person willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work.
2. Full employment implies that frictional unemployment cannot exist.
3. Structural unemployment may still exist at full employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Full employment means that everyone willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work, but frictional and structural unemployment may still exist.
tq: Reject the absolute claim that full employment eliminates every form of unemployment.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: The natural rate of unemployment is composed of:
x: The natural rate is the combination of frictional and structural unemployment existing at full employment.
tq: Recall the exact components of a standard composite concept.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: The concept of the natural rate of unemployment is particularly associated with:
x: The concept of the natural rate of unemployment is associated with Milton Friedman.
tq: Link the named economist with the specific concept rather than a related curve or law.
sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

s: Technological unemployment is best understood as:
o: Job loss caused exclusively by a fall in aggregate demand
Unemployment caused by a worker voluntarily rejecting the prevailing wage
Temporary unemployment during the agricultural off-season
Job loss caused by changes in technology and treated as a subtype of structural unemployment
x: Technological unemployment results from technological change and is a subtype of structural unemployment.
tq: Use the cause-and-classification link to distinguish technological from cyclical unemployment.

s:
Which of the following correctly describes the likely labour-market effect of automation and artificial intelligence?
1. Automation in manufacturing may reduce demand for low-skilled and routine jobs.
2. Artificial intelligence in services may reduce demand for routine jobs.
3. Technological change can generate structural unemployment.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Automation in manufacturing and AI in services can reduce demand for low-skilled and routine jobs, and the resulting technological unemployment is structural in character.
tq: Combine the sector-specific examples with their common structural effect.

s: Jobless growth is more likely when economic growth is driven mainly by:
o: Labour-intensive manufacturing rather than capital-intensive activities
Capital-intensive sectors such as information technology and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing
x: Growth led by capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance, instead of labour-intensive manufacturing, can produce jobless growth.
tq: Focus on the reversed capital-intensive versus labour-intensive comparison.

s: The Phillips curve was named after A.W. Phillips, whose relevant work dates to:
x: The Phillips curve is named after A.W. Phillips and is associated with his 1958 work.
tq: Use the date-specific option rather than confusing it with later developments of the theory.

s: The traditional trade-off between inflation and unemployment breaks down in a situation of:
o: Stable prices with potential output growth
Stagflation, characterised by high inflation and high unemployment
x: Stagflation combines high inflation with high unemployment and therefore breaks down the traditional Phillips-curve trade-off.
tq: Identify the unusual combination that contradicts the traditional inverse relationship.

s:
Consider the following statements about the long-run Phillips curve:
1. It is vertical at the natural rate of unemployment.
2. The long-run formulation is associated with Friedman and Phelps.
3. It establishes a permanent trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The long-run Phillips curve is vertical at the natural rate and is associated with Friedman and Phelps. It does not establish a permanent trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
tq: Separate the short-run trade-off from the long-run vertical-curve proposition.

s: According to Okun's law, a one percentage point rise in unemployment above the natural rate is associated approximately with:
o: A 2% rise in output above potential GDP
A 1% rise in output above potential GDP
A 2% fall in output below potential GDP
A 5% fall in output below potential GDP
x: Okun's law states that a one percentage point increase in unemployment above the natural rate is associated with roughly a 2% reduction in output below potential GDP.
tq: Track both parts of the quantitative relationship: the unemployment point and the output percentage.

s: Okun's law is associated with:
x: The inverse relationship between unemployment and the gap between actual and potential output is known as Okun's law, associated with Arthur Okun.
tq: Match the economic law with its principal economist.

s: According to the monthly PLFS data cited for May 2026, India's unemployment rate was:
x: The monthly PLFS unemployment rate rose to 5.5% in May 2026 from 5.2% in April 2026.
tq: Distinguish the current-month value from the immediately preceding month and other comparative figures.

s: Which one of the following correctly presents the monthly PLFS unemployment-rate movement cited for India?
o: It rose from 3.2% in April 2026 to 4.1% in May 2026.
It declined from 5.5% in April 2026 to 5.2% in May 2026.
It remained unchanged at 5.2% during April and May 2026.
It rose from 5.2% in April 2026 to 5.5% in May 2026.
x: The unemployment rate increased from 5.2% in April 2026 to 5.5% in May 2026.
tq: Check the direction of change as well as the two month-specific figures.

s: For May 2026, the rural and urban unemployment rates cited for India were respectively:
x: The cited May 2026 rates were 5.1% for rural areas and 6.4% for urban areas.
tq: Preserve the order of the paired rural and urban figures.

s: Which statement regarding seasonal labour migration is correct?
o: Nearly 30–35 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
Nearly 3–5 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
More than 100 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
Nearly 10–15 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
x: Approximately 30–35 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
tq: Identify the stated range rather than selecting a nearby but incorrect magnitude.

s: The unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh, compared with the all-India rate cited for the PLFS 2023–24 and APSES 2024–25 comparison, was:
x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 4.1% unemployment compared with 3.2% for India, making the AP rate higher by 0.9 percentage points.
tq: Subtract the paired rates and retain the direction of the comparison.

s:
Which of the following correctly states the unemployment indicators for Andhra Pradesh cited in the comparison?
1. Overall unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh was 4.1%.
2. Youth unemployment rate for the 15–29 age group was 17.5%.
3. Urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All three figures are correct: overall unemployment was 4.1%, youth unemployment for ages 15–29 was 17.5%, and urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%.
tq: Use the all-inclusive option after verifying each age- and gender-specific figure.

s: In the overall gender-wise unemployment figures cited for Andhra Pradesh, which comparison is correct?
o: Female and male unemployment were both 4.1%.
Female unemployment was 29.1% and male unemployment was 17.5%.
Female unemployment was 3.7% and male unemployment was 4.3%.
Female unemployment was 4.3% and male unemployment was 3.7%.
x: The cited overall figures were 3.7% for females and 4.3% for males.
tq: Avoid reversing the two gender-specific values.

s: A decline in the measured unemployment rate may fail to indicate genuine job creation when it results from:
o: A rise in potential GDP caused by technology
A permanent reduction in the labour force due to higher wages
x: A falling unemployment rate may reflect people entering low-productivity work under distress rather than the creation of good or adequate jobs.
tq: Distinguish an apparently favourable indicator from its possible underlying labour-market condition.

s: Which of the following comparisons between India and developed countries is correct?
o: India mainly faces cyclical unemployment, whereas developed countries mainly face disguised unemployment.
Developed countries mainly face seasonal unemployment, whereas India mainly faces classical unemployment.
India mainly faces structural and disguised unemployment, whereas developed countries mainly face cyclical, demand-deficient unemployment.
Both India and developed countries mainly face only frictional unemployment.
x: India's unemployment is characterised as structural and disguised, while developed countries are described as facing mainly cyclical or demand-deficient unemployment.
tq: Keep both sides of the comparative classification aligned with the stated economic context.

s: Which economist is associated with the explanation of cyclical unemployment in developed countries as demand-deficient unemployment?
x: The demand-deficiency explanation of cyclical unemployment is associated with Keynes.
tq: Match the explanatory framework with the economist associated with it.
